item.title: Billund Airport passengers fell significantly in 2025
item.description: In 2025, total departing passengers from Danish public airports reached a record high of nearly 19 million, a 5 percent increase. Copenhagen Airport drove this growth with 16.2 million departing passengers, an 8 percent rise, totaling 32.4 million travelers. item.title: Danish media association to sue OpenAI
item.description: The Danish organization DPCMO, representing 99 percent of the country’s news media, is suing the American company OpenAI. The lawsuit alleges that OpenAI used Danish media content to train ChatGPT until at least summer 2024, even though media outlets could only opt out starting in summer 2023. The dispute also concerns ChatGPT reproducing news articles […]

item.title: Troels Lund Poulsen won’t participate in a government that implements a wealth tax
item.description: Venstre chairman Troels Lund Poulsen has declared that he will not participate in a government that introduces a wealth tax, arguing it would make Denmark poorer and undermine the economy. item.title: Gray and wet weather will dominate the weekend
item.description: The upcoming weekend in Denmark will be mostly gray and wet, according to DMI meteorologist Hans Peter Wandler. Friday begins with clouds and rain for most, with five to ten millimeters expected and temperatures between six and 12 degrees. item.title: The government says it wants to limit the number of Ukrainians in Denmark
item.description: People from 14 Ukrainian regions will no longer be able to obtain a residence permit in Denmark under the so-called special law. This is the third action this week by Social Democrat minister Rasmus Stoklund targeting internationals living in Denmark.

item.title: What we vote for, who can vote, and how the Danish political system works: everything you need to know about the upcoming national election
item.description: Yesterday, Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen called for the election, which will take place on March 24. Who is eligible to vote? Who can run? What are we voting for? Who appoints the prime minister? What happens after the election? Here is everything you need to know.

item.title: Historic church Helligåndskirken reopens in the heart of Copenhagen after two years of renovation
item.description: The funding allowed the church to replace an unstable wooden floor, which had been covered with needle felt carpet, with a stone floor in the nave. The church also installed a new heating system, and its furnishings were carefully restored.

item.title: Denmark first in EU to end mother-to-child HIV transmission
item.description: Denmark is the first country in the EU to eliminate mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis, according to Statens Serum Institut (SSI). For years, Denmark has conducted regular screening of pregnant women and ensured rapid treatment, meaning children are no longer born with these infections.
